draft.title: Dev/SRE Toolbox — in-process modular toolbox for the existing FastAPI app (revised)
draft.summary: Add a self-contained `app/toolbox/` package (Tool protocol + explicit static registry + three pure analysis modules) plus a thin `app/routers/toolbox.py` router mounted at the repository's flat `/api/toolbox` prefix and gated by the existing `verify_credentials` Basic-Auth dependency, typed Pydantic models in `app/models/toolbox.py`, env-driven limits in `app/config/settings.py`, one new dependency (PyYAML, safe loader only), tests in the base layer, and one numbered doc. No new service, database, queue, broker, observability stack or CI change (`.github/workflows/**` is a protected path). CPU-bound parsing is offloaded with `loop.run_in_executor`, matching `/api/fib/{x}`. Findings are never HTTP errors. This revision fixes the issues raised on the previous draft: (a) the YAML depth limit is enforced by a `SafeLoader` subclass that counts `compose_node` recursion, and an explicit alias/anchor budget is added; (b) `k8s.manifest.inspect` returns `outcome=fail` only when at least one error-severity finding exists, `warn` for warning-only, `pass` otherwise, so missing configuration is not conflated with risky configuration; (c) an unknown tool id returns a direct `JSONResponse(404, {"error": "Unknown tool", "tool": ...})` that bypasses the app-wide 404 handler; (d) `.validate` actively rejects URL/path-like input; (e) `toolbox_enabled` defaults to `true`; (f) docs carry authenticated curl examples, a finding-code reference table and Diátaxis section headings; (g) a README.md pointer is added.

tests/test_toolbox_tools.py, tests/test_toolbox_api.py, tests/test_toolbox_k8s.py plus the untouched existing suite as regression.
Only a SafeLoader subclass is used; no yaml.load, no python/object tags, no arbitrary object construction.

Settings fields toolbox_max_input_bytes / _yaml_documents / _yaml_depth / _yaml_aliases / _findings / _diff_context_lines; violations raise ToolboxLimitExceeded -> HTTP 413 naming the limit; documented in docs/14 with no silent truncation.

contracts: GET /api/toolbox/tools -> 200 [ToolDescriptor{id, description, version, input_schema}] (input_schema is the tool input model's JSON schema).
POST /api/toolbox/runs body {tool: str, input: object} -> 200 ToolRunResponse{run_id, tool, tool_version, status, outcome, summary{info,warning,error}, findings[], output, duration_ms}.
status is the execution status: "completed" when the tool returned a result, "failed" only when the tool raised unexpectedly (which is surfaced as HTTP 500, not 200).

outcome is the analysis verdict, tool-defined: json.validate -> pass|fail; text.diff -> pass; k8s.manifest.inspect -> fail when at least one finding has severity error, warn when only info/warning findings exist, pass when there are no findings. Missing configuration (warning) is therefore not conflated with explicitly risky configuration (error).
Finding{code, severity: info|warning|error, message, location{document_index, resource_kind, resource_name, path}, suggestion}.
Findings are never HTTP errors: a manifest with errors still returns HTTP 200 with outcome=fail.
Request validation: malformed outer body or malformed tool input -> HTTP 422 with FastAPI's {"detail": [...]} shape (the app's existing validation handling).
Unknown tool id -> HTTP 404 with a direct JSONResponse body {"error": "Unknown tool", "tool": "<id>"} that bypasses the app-wide 404 handler.
Limit violation -> HTTP 413 with {"error": "<limit name> exceeded", "limit": "<setting name>", "limit_value": <int>}; never a truncated result.
Unexpected internal error -> HTTP 500 with {"error": "Internal server error", "run_id": "<uuid>"}; no traceback, no payload.
Tool protocol: run(payload: BaseModel, limits: ToolboxLimits) -> ToolResult, pure, no FastAPI import, no IO, no network, deterministic ordering of findings.
Logging contract: one structured loguru record per run with run_id, tool, tool_version, status, outcome, finding counts and duration_ms; never the payload, manifest, diff or resource names.

draft.migration_rollback: No data migration: the feature is stateless, adds no table, no Alembic revision and no background worker, so there is nothing to migrate. Deployment is a normal application rollout; the only new runtime dependency is PyYAML, which must be present in the image before the new code is served. Rollback is a plain revert of the change set: remove app/toolbox/, app/models/toolbox.py and app/routers/toolbox.py, drop the include_router line and the new Settings fields, and remove the PyYAML pin. Because the router is additive and no existing route, model or middleware is modified, a revert restores the previous behaviour with no residual state. The feature can also be disabled without a revert by setting toolbox_enabled=false, which skips router registration.

tradeoffs: Flat /api/toolbox instead of the literal /api/v1/toolbox: consistent with every existing router and with the mandate's 'adapt the prefix' clause, at the cost of not introducing a versioning scheme the repository does not use.

Unknown tool returns a direct JSONResponse(404) with the tool id rather than the app-wide envelope: more informative for the caller, at the cost of a body shape that differs from the generic 404 handler.

Limit violations use 413 rather than 400: avoids the app-wide 400 handler that would collapse the body, at the cost of a status code that is semantically 'payload too large' for non-size limits such as the findings cap; the structured limit field disambiguates.
Findings cap aborts the run instead of truncating: satisfies 'no silent truncation' and keeps the result trustworthy, at the cost of refusing to analyse very noisy manifests.

outcome has three values (pass/warn/fail) rather than two: distinguishes missing configuration from explicitly risky configuration at the top level, at the cost of a slightly richer contract than the mandate's example.
PyYAML added as a dependency: required for safe YAML parsing and not currently present; it is a library, not a framework, database or broker.

No custom Prometheus metric per tool: the existing prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator already exports invocations, error status codes and duration per route, so no second metric registry is introduced; per-tool counters would be a small follow-up if per-tool dashboards are needed.
Executor offload with a timeout: keeps the event loop free and bounds the request, but a timed-out worker thread may finish in the background — documented as a limitation.
Tool input validation reuses FastAPI's 422 {"detail": [...]} shape rather than a bespoke envelope: consistent with the app, but the body is less self-describing than a custom error object.
No GET /runs/{id}: the mandate forbids it without real persistence, so run_id is correlation-only and no in-memory store is faked as durable.

draft.title: Dev/SRE Toolbox: modular, synchronous, read-only utility catalog inside the existing FastAPI app (rev. 2)
draft.summary: Add a self-contained `app/toolbox/` package (Tool protocol + explicit registry + three pure analysis functions), a thin `app/routers/toolbox.py` mounted at the repository's flat `/api/toolbox` prefix behind the existing `verify_credentials` Basic-Auth dependency, typed Pydantic models in `app/models/toolbox.py`, and env-driven limits in `app/config/settings.py`. One new dependency only: PyYAML, used exclusively through a custom `yaml.SafeLoader` subclass that enforces a nesting-depth budget and an alias/anchor expansion budget (so `toolbox_max_yaml_depth` is enforced during composition, not after parsing, and billion-laughs expansion is bounded). CPU-bound parsing is dispatched with `loop.run_in_executor` exactly as `/api/fib/{x}` already does, wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for` with a configurable timeout. No database, no queue, no migration, no new service, no new observability stack and no new metric families: run_id is correlation-only, logs go through the existing loguru setup, and invocation/error/duration visibility is already provided by the installed prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator. Controlled limit/unknown-tool errors are returned as explicit JSONResponse objects (413/404) so the app-wide 400/404 handlers cannot collapse them into `{"error": "Bad request"}` / `{"error": "Not found"}`. `json.validate` parses inline text only and does not use a URL/path prefix heuristic (the input schema has no URL/path field, so nothing is fetched or read).

assumptions.text: The toolbox router is mounted at the flat prefix /api/toolbox (not /api/v1/toolbox), because every existing router uses prefix '/api' and the mandate says to adapt the prefix to the repository's conventions. If the reviewer insists on the literal /api/v1/toolbox, only the APIRouter prefix string and the docs change.

PyYAML is added to requirements.txt and used exclusively through a custom yaml.SafeLoader subclass. The exact pin is chosen at implementation time against the version available to the build; no YAML parser is present today, so this is a demonstrable need and not a gratuitous framework. If the pin cannot be resolved in the build environment, the k8s tool cannot be delivered and that is reported as an obstacle with evidence.

The configurable YAML depth limit is enforced during composition by overriding compose_node in a SafeLoader subclass (depth counter incremented on entry, decremented on exit, ToolLimitExceeded raised above the budget), and alias/anchor expansion is bounded by counting AliasEvent occurrences against a configurable alias budget, so a nested-anchor document (billion laughs) yields a controlled 413 rather than an unbounded structure.

Exceeding the findings cap returns HTTP 413 with a message naming the limit rather than truncating the list, because the mandate forbids silent truncation and requires controlled errors for inputs exceeding limits.
outcome is 'fail' when at least one finding has severity 'warning' or 'error', otherwise 'pass'; text.diff always yields 'pass' because it is a transformation, not an analysis.

The result contract's 'status' enum keeps 'failed' reserved; in this MVP every HTTP 200 body carries status='completed', and an unexpected internal error is reported as HTTP 500 with a sanitized envelope instead of a 200 body.

The 500 envelope is {"error": "Internal server error", "detail": "run_id=<uuid>"}: the run_id is a correlation identifier, not an internal detail, and it is the only way the client can tie a failure to the server log line.

No type checker (mypy/pyright) is configured in the repository, so the 'type checking' command required by the mandate cannot be run; this is reported as an obstacle with evidence rather than as a pass.

No per-tool metric module is added: the installed prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator already exports invocations, error status codes and duration per route, so adding Counter/Histogram families would be superfluous surface and would risk duplicate-registration errors when create_app() is called repeatedly in tests. The mandate's metrics clause is satisfied by the existing exporter.
The toolbox endpoints are protected with the existing verify_credentials Basic-Auth dependency at router level, matching /api/debug/* and /api/mgmt/threaddump; no new auth mechanism is introduced.

Controlled errors (unknown tool, limit exceeded) are returned as explicit JSONResponse objects from the endpoint rather than raised as HTTPException(400/404), because the app-wide handlers would otherwise collapse them to the fixed 'Bad request' / 'Not found' envelopes.

The run endpoint wraps the run_in_executor dispatch in asyncio.wait_for with a configurable timeout (toolbox_run_timeout_seconds), so a pathological in-limit input cannot hold a default-executor thread indefinitely.

json.validate does not use a URL/path prefix heuristic: its input schema exposes only an inline text field, so URLs and file paths are not accepted as inputs and nothing is fetched or read. This avoids false negatives on syntactically valid JSON strings that happen to look like a URL or path.

tradeoffs: Flat prefix /api/toolbox instead of the literal /api/v1/toolbox: consistent with /api/debug and /api/mgmt, but deviates from the example path in the mandate; the mandate's 'adapt the prefix to the repository's conventions' clause is the justification.
Rejecting over-limit findings with 413 instead of truncating: fully explicit and non-silent, but a very large manifest yields no findings at all rather than a partial list.

Returning controlled errors as JSONResponse objects instead of raising HTTPException: preserves the specific message, but means the toolbox does not use the app-wide 400/404 handlers and the behaviour must be documented.
Adding PyYAML: a new third-party dependency, but unavoidable for safe YAML parsing and far smaller than any alternative (no ruamel, no schema library).

Synchronous execution with run_in_executor wrapped in asyncio.wait_for: satisfies the 'no queue' constraint and keeps the MVP small, but a very large manifest occupies a thread-pool slot for the duration of the request and a timeout yields a controlled error rather than a partial result.

No per-tool metric families: keeps the /metrics surface unchanged and avoids duplicate-registration risk, at the cost of per-tool invocation counters (route-level metrics from the existing instrumentator remain available).
Keeping 'status' as an enum with a reserved 'failed' value: preserves the documented contract shape for a future asynchronous mode, at the cost of an unused value in the MVP.
Dropping the json.validate URL/path heuristic: avoids false negatives on valid JSON strings, at the cost of not actively refusing URL-like text (which is harmless because nothing is fetched or read).

draft.summary: Add a self-contained `app/toolbox/` package (Tool protocol + explicit dict registry + three pure analysis modules) and one new router `app/routers/toolbox.py` mounted at `/api/toolbox` inside the existing `create_app()` factory, protected by the existing `verify_credentials` Basic-Auth dependency. Contract models (RunRequest, RunResponse, Finding, FindingLocation, FindingSummary, ToolInfo) are added to the existing `app/models/schemas.py`; limits are added as Pydantic Settings fields. PyYAML is the only new dependency, pinned explicitly and used exclusively through a depth- and node-budget-guarded `yaml.SafeLoader` subclass that also bounds alias/anchor expansion. CPU-bound parsing is dispatched with `loop.run_in_executor` (mirroring `/api/fib/{x}`) and wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for` with a configurable timeout. No database, queue, broker, migration, persistence or new observability stack is introduced; `run_id` is correlation-only. Error channels are kept distinct and are returned as explicit `JSONResponse` objects so the app-wide 400/404 handlers cannot rewrite them: unknown tool -> 404 `{"error": "Unknown tool", "tool": <id>}`; limit breach -> 413 `{"error": ..., "limit": ..., "limit_value": ...}` (documented as covering all toolbox limits, not only payload size); malformed body -> FastAPI 422; unexpected failure -> 500 `{"error": "Internal server error", "run_id": <id>}`. Findings are never HTTP errors: syntactically invalid JSON/YAML yields `status=completed`, `outcome=fail` and a finding carrying line/column. `json.validate` actively rejects URL- or path-like input with a controlled finding rather than merely omitting a URL/path parameter.

tradeoffs: Prefix /api/toolbox instead of the literal /api/v1/toolbox: follows the repository's flat /api/<area> convention and the mandate's instruction to adapt the prefix, at the cost of not introducing API versioning that the rest of the app does not have.

Contract models added to the existing app/models/schemas.py rather than a new models module: keeps one source of truth for Pydantic models as the repository does, at the cost of a slightly larger shared module.

Limit breaches return 413 with a structured body instead of the app-wide 400 envelope: preserves the information the mandate requires (which limit, what value) but introduces a second error shape alongside {"error": "Bad request"}; 413 is documented as covering all toolbox limits, not only payload size.

Unknown tool returns an explicit JSONResponse 404 with {"error": "Unknown tool", "tool": ...} rather than a 200 with status=failed: treats an unknown identifier as a request error, not an analysis result, and keeps the {"error": ...} convention; the explicit JSONResponse is required because the app-wide 404 handler would otherwise collapse the body.

PyYAML added as a dependency: unavoidable for safe YAML parsing, but it is a new third-party library in a repository that currently has none for YAML; the alternative (hand-written YAML subset parser) would be far larger and less safe.

Depth guard plus node budget implemented as a SafeLoader subclass rather than a post-parse measurement: stronger against deeply nested and alias-amplified input, at the cost of a small amount of loader plumbing.

Synchronous execution with run_in_executor wrapped in asyncio.wait_for rather than a queue: matches the mandate and the existing Fibonacci pattern, and bounds thread occupancy; a very large manifest still occupies a thread-pool slot for up to the timeout — mitigated by the input-size, document-count, depth and node limits.

Router mounted unconditionally rather than behind a feature flag: the mandate requires the tools to be available and the endpoints are Basic-Auth protected; a flag would add configuration surface with no demonstrated need.
No GET /runs/{id}: the mandate forbids it without real persistence, so run_id is deliberately correlation-only and no in-memory run store is introduced.

findings.title: json.validate URL/path prefix heuristic can reject valid JSON
findings.detail: Proposal A states json.validate 'actively rejects URL- or path-like input with a controlled finding' (JSON_INPUT_NOT_INLINE). The mandate only requires that the tool not accept URLs or file paths as inputs (no fetch, no read); it also requires returning the parsed value for syntactically valid JSON. A prefix/heuristic match on text that is itself a valid JSON string value (e.g. a string containing a filesystem path) would return outcome=fail for input that is syntactically valid, contradicting the 'returns the parsed value' clause. Proposal C's schema-only interpretation avoids this. Recommend dropping the heuristic or restricting it to non-JSON-looking input.

claims.statement: Proposal A's json.validate rejects URL/path-like text by prefix/heuristic matching, which can reject syntactically valid JSON string values.

findings.title: No dedicated regression test module for existing endpoints
findings.detail: Proposal B's change list adds tests/test_toolbox_tools.py, tests/test_toolbox_api.py and tests/test_toolbox_k8s.py but no regression test module; it relies on re-running the existing suite. The mandate explicitly asks for regression tests that verify the existing endpoints keep working. Re-running the existing suite is acceptable, but a dedicated assertion that the toolbox addition did not change existing route paths would be stronger.

claims.statement: The management test asserts specific route paths are present in /api/mgmt/mappings, so adding routes must not break route flattening.

findings.title: Catalog response is an object, not the list the mandate describes
findings.detail: Proposal C returns ToolCatalogResponse {tools: [...]} from GET /api/toolbox/tools. The mandate describes the endpoint as a 'List of the available tools' with identifier, description, version and input schema, so a bare JSON array is the natural shape. The wrapper is a contract deviation that must be documented and tested.

claims.statement: The mandate describes GET /api/v1/toolbox/tools as a 'List of the available tools', so a bare JSON array is the natural response shape.

findings.title: outcome=fail for warning-only findings weakens the missing-vs-risky distinction
findings.detail: Proposal C sets outcome=fail when at least one finding has severity warning or error. A manifest whose only findings are missing-configuration warnings is therefore reported as fail, even though the mandate requires missing configuration to be distinguished from explicitly risky configuration. Proposal C does add a `category` field to distinguish them, but the top-level outcome still conflates the two.

claims.statement: The mandate requires the k8s tool to distinguish missing configuration from explicitly risky configuration; reporting outcome=fail for warning-only findings weakens that distinction at the top level.

findings.title: 500 body embeds run_id inside a 'detail' string
findings.detail: Proposal C returns 500 {"error": "Internal server error", "detail": "run_id=<uuid>"}. The mandated result contract has no 'detail' field, and mixing a correlation id into a free-text detail string is awkward for clients that want to read the run_id programmatically. Proposal A and B return run_id as its own field.

claims.statement: The mandated result contract has no 'detail' field on the error envelope, and run_id is a correlation id rather than an internal detail.

findings.title: Drops the URL/path heuristic; divergence from the other proposals
findings.detail: Proposal C deliberately does not reject URL/path-like strings, arguing that the input schema exposes only an inline text field so nothing is fetched or read. This is a defensible reading of 'does not accept URLs or file paths', but it diverges from Proposal A and B and from a literal reading; the choice should be documented and tested (a URL-like string that is not valid JSON must still yield outcome=fail).

claims.statement: The mandate says json.validate does not accept URLs or file paths; an inline-text-only schema satisfies this without a heuristic.

findings.title: PyYAML becomes a hard application-startup dependency, not just a toolbox dependency
findings.detail: The toolbox router is imported at module scope in app/main.py and the k8s tool imports PyYAML, so a missing/uninstallable PyYAML raises ImportError inside create_app() and takes down the whole application, not only the toolbox routes. The proposal pins PyYAML==6.0.2 (good for reproducibility) but does not state a deployment guard: the image must be rebuilt from requirements.txt before the new code is served, and the declared test command `python -m pytest -q` will fail at import if the package is absent. Recommend an explicit pre-deploy check that `python -c "import yaml"` succeeds in the target image, and consider importing the toolbox router defensively so a missing optional dependency degrades only the toolbox.

claims.statement: requirements.txt declares no YAML parsing library today, so PyYAML is a genuinely new runtime dependency.
app/main.py registers routers via include_router inside create_app(), so a toolbox import failure aborts application startup.

findings.title: Timed-out executor task keeps running and can exhaust the default thread pool
findings.detail: asyncio.wait_for cancels the awaiting coroutine but cannot cancel the thread running tool.run in the default executor. Under repeated timeouts (or a burst of large-but-in-limit manifests) the default ThreadPoolExecutor can be saturated, degrading unrelated endpoints that also use run_in_executor (e.g. /api/fib/{x}). The proposal documents the limitation but adds no mitigation beyond input limits. Recommend a bounded, dedicated executor for toolbox runs and/or a documented concurrency cap, and an alert on toolbox timeout rate.

claims.statement: app/routers/api.py offloads CPU-bound work with loop.run_in_executor, sharing the default executor with the toolbox runner.

findings.title: No operational kill switch: router is mounted unconditionally
findings.detail: The toolbox router is always registered, so disabling the feature in production requires a code revert and redeploy. The endpoints are Basic-Auth protected, which limits exposure, but an operator has no runtime lever if the tool misbehaves. A single settings flag gating include_router (defaulting to enabled) would give a reversible operational control at negligible cost.

claims.statement: app/main.py registers routers via include_router inside create_app().

findings.title: HTTP 413 is reused for non-size limits (findings cap, depth, document count)

This is documented, but it complicates monitoring/alerting semantics (a 413 no longer implies a large body) and may confuse clients. Acceptable for the MVP if the structured body names the limit; ensure dashboards/alerts key on the body's `limit` field rather than the status code alone.

claims.statement: app/main.py installs a global 400 handler returning the fixed envelope {"error": "Bad request"}, which is why the toolbox must use a different status for controlled limit errors.

findings.title: json.validate rejects URL/path-like input by string heuristic, which is not a security control and can reject valid JSON
findings.detail: Proposal A states json.validate 'actively rejects URL- or path-like input with a controlled finding'. The mandate only requires that the tool accept JSON text and not accept URLs or file paths as inputs; the safe way to satisfy that is to expose only an inline `text` field and never fetch or read anything. A prefix/heuristic rejection adds no trust-boundary protection (nothing is fetched either way) and introduces false negatives: a syntactically valid JSON string that happens to start with a scheme or path-like prefix would be reported as a finding instead of being parsed. This is input validation by pattern matching, which is fragile and not a substitute for the real control (no network, no file IO).

claims.statement: json.validate rejects inputs by prefix/heuristic matching of URL schemes or path-like strings.
json.validate performs no network call and no file read; it only parses the inline text field.

findings.title: YAML depth and alias/anchor expansion must be bounded during composition, not after parsing
findings.detail: The k8s tool parses untrusted YAML. A SafeLoader prevents arbitrary object construction but does not by itself bound nesting depth or alias/anchor amplification (billion-laughs), which are DoS vectors on a synchronous, CPU-bound endpoint. Proposal A relies on a node budget plus a compose_node recursion counter; the proposal does not state that the depth counter is enforced during composition (before the structure is materialised) nor that alias expansion is bounded independently of the input-size limit. If depth is only measured after parsing, a deeply nested document can still exhaust the stack or memory before the check runs. The limit must abort during composition and surface a controlled error.

claims.statement: The YAML depth limit is enforced during node composition (before the document is materialised), not measured after parsing.
Alias/anchor expansion is bounded by a dedicated budget independent of the input-size limit.

findings.title: Input-size limit is applied to the parsed string, so the full body is buffered before rejection
findings.detail: toolbox_max_input_bytes is checked on the decoded string. FastAPI reads and buffers the whole request body before the handler runs, so an oversized body is still fully materialised in memory before the limit fires. The mandate requires configurable input-size limits and controlled rejection; the proposal should state where the size check happens relative to body buffering, and whether the existing app-wide body cap (as used by the debug echo endpoints) is reused.

claims.statement: The toolbox input-size limit is enforced before the full request body is buffered, or the residual buffering is documented.

findings.title: Payload logging must be verified against the existing request-logging middleware, not only the new log line
findings.detail: The mandate forbids logging payloads, manifests, diffs or possible secrets. Proposal A constrains its own loguru line, but the toolbox routes also pass through the app-wide request-logging middleware. If that middleware records request bodies, manifests and diffs would be logged regardless of the new code. The proposal must confirm the middleware does not log bodies for these routes, or the data-flow requirement is not met.

claims.statement: No request payload, manifest, diff or secret is written to logs by the toolbox code path, including the app-wide request-logging middleware.

findings.title: CPU-bound endpoints may be unthrottled because slowapi has no middleware or per-route decorator
findings.detail: Proposal A records that slowapi default_limits are configured but no SlowAPIMiddleware or per-route decorator is present, so rate limiting may not be enforced. The toolbox adds CPU-bound, synchronous endpoints that occupy default-executor threads; without throttling they are a DoS surface. This is a pre-existing condition, but the proposal should state the residual exposure rather than assume the default limit applies.

claims.statement: The toolbox endpoints are subject to an enforced rate limit, or the absence of enforcement is documented as a residual risk.

findings.title: json.validate rejects URL/path-like input by heuristic instead of relying on the absence of a fetch/read capability
findings.detail: Proposal B states json_validate.py 'rejects URL/path-like input before parsing'. As with Proposal A, this is pattern matching rather than a trust-boundary control: the tool never fetches or reads, so the only real requirement is that the input model expose inline text and nothing else. The heuristic can reject valid JSON that resembles a URL or path, producing a false finding. The mandate's 'does not accept URLs or file paths' is satisfied structurally by the input schema, not by string matching.

claims.statement: json.validate rejects inputs by prefix/heuristic matching of URL schemes or path-like strings.
json.validate performs no network call and no file read; it only parses the inline text field.

findings.title: YAML depth and alias budget must abort during composition and be independently bounded
findings.detail: Proposal B adds a SafeLoader subclass with a compose_node recursion counter and an alias budget. The proposal must state that the depth counter is enforced during composition (before the structure is materialised) and that the alias budget is independent of the input-size limit; otherwise a deeply nested or alias-amplified document can exhaust stack or memory before any post-parse check runs. This is the primary DoS vector for the synchronous k8s endpoint.

claims.statement: The YAML depth limit is enforced during node composition (before the document is materialised), not measured after parsing.
Alias/anchor expansion is bounded by a dedicated budget independent of the input-size limit.

findings.title: Payload logging must be verified against the existing request-logging middleware
findings.detail: Proposal B constrains its own loguru record but the toolbox routes also traverse the app-wide request-logging middleware. If that middleware logs request bodies, manifests and diffs would be logged despite the new code. The proposal must confirm the middleware does not log bodies for these routes.

claims.statement: No request payload, manifest, diff or secret is written to logs by the toolbox code path, including the app-wide request-logging middleware.

findings.title: Input-size limit is applied after the body is buffered
findings.detail: As in Proposal A, toolbox_max_input_bytes is checked on the decoded string, so an oversized body is fully buffered before rejection. The proposal should state where the size check happens relative to body buffering and whether the existing app-wide body cap is reused.

claims.statement: The toolbox input-size limit is enforced before the full request body is buffered, or the residual buffering is documented.

findings.title: CPU-bound endpoints may be unthrottled because slowapi has no middleware or per-route decorator
findings.detail: Proposal B records that slowapi default_limits are configured but no SlowAPIMiddleware or per-route decorator is present. The new synchronous, CPU-bound endpoints occupy default-executor threads; without throttling they are a DoS surface. The residual exposure should be stated rather than assumed covered.

claims.statement: The toolbox endpoints are subject to an enforced rate limit, or the absence of enforcement is documented as a residual risk.

findings.title: Contradictory outcome semantics between coverage and assumption
findings.detail: Proposal C's coverage for req-2448feaf8d7c8dc7 states 'outcome is fail only on error-severity findings', while assumption asm-b8f7274f9059050e states 'outcome is fail when at least one finding has severity warning or error'. findings.title: text.diff worker thread is not cancellable when the run timeout fires
findings.detail: app/toolbox/tools/text_diff.py calls difflib.unified_diff, whose worst case is quadratic in the input size, on inputs bounded only by TOOLBOX_MAX_INPUT_BYTES (default 262144 bytes per side). The router wraps the executor call in asyncio.wait_for, but a timed-out run_in_executor future cannot cancel the underlying thread, so a pathological diff keeps a worker thread busy after the client receives 504. Bounded input keeps the impact low; this is a resource-exhaustion note, not a correctness bug.

claims.statement: text.diff uses difflib.unified_diff

The check should require a digest of the form '@sha256:<hex>'.

findings.title: Run timeout returns 504 but does not cancel the CPU-bound worker thread
findings.detail: The plan states the tool run is dispatched with loop.run_in_executor and wrapped in asyncio.wait_for with TOOLBOX_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. asyncio.wait_for cancels the awaiting coroutine, not the thread executing the tool: on timeout the client receives 504 while the parsing work keeps running to completion in the shared default ThreadPoolExecutor (the same executor used by /api/fib/{x}). My assessment therefore covers only the visible portion; the missing files are an evidence gap, not a proven defect (the initial checks show the app imports and the toolbox tests run, so `main.py`, `settings.py` and `models/toolbox.py` must exist and be wired).

What the visible code does well and matches the mandate: the toolbox is a self-contained `app/toolbox/` package with a `Tool` Protocol, an explicit import-time registry with a duplicate-id `RuntimeError`, and three pure-Python tools that never import FastAPI (`app/toolbox/base.py`, `registry.py`, `tools/*.py`). YAML is parsed through a `yaml.SafeLoader` subclass that enforces a composition-depth budget and an alias budget during composition, plus a cycle-aware `_assert_object_depth` walk over the composed graph; no `eval`/`exec`/shell/dynamic import/network/file access appears. Limits (input bytes, YAML documents, depth, aliases, findings, diff context lines) are carried in a frozen `ToolLimits` dataclass and exceeded limits raise `ToolLimitExceeded` (no silent truncation). The router dispatches `tool.run` via `loop.run_in_executor` wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for`, generates a `run_id`, logs `run_id/tool/status/outcome/duration_ms` without payload, and returns sanitized 500 (`run_id` only) and 404/413/422/504 as explicit `JSONResponse` objects so the app-wide 400/404 handlers cannot collapse them. Findings are returned inside a 200 `ToolRunResponse`, never as HTTP errors; invalid JSON and invalid YAML produce negative analysis results (`JSON_INVALID_SYNTAX`, `K8S_INVALID_YAML`) rather than HTTP errors. The k8s tool covers all seven mandated check families, distinguishes `missing_configuration` from `risky_configuration`, skips probe checks for init containers while still inspecting them, and carries a `DISCLAIMER` stating the checks are neither a complete Kubernetes validation nor a security certification. Initial checks report `project.build` PASS, `project.test` PASS (133 passed, 25 skipped), `project.lint` PASS (0).

Overall: the visible implementation is coherent, deterministic (only `run_id`/`duration_ms` vary), and consistent with the approved plan. I have not seen DEV1's handoff; the concerns below are the items I would want resolved or explicitly accepted before I can sign off, and several are unverifiable from the truncated diff.
concerns: Diff is truncated: the top of `app/routers/toolbox.py` (imports, `_effective_limits`, `GET /tools`, router prefix and `verify_credentials` dependency) is not visible, so the catalog contract, the auth wiring and the `/api/toolbox` prefix cannot be verified from the diff alone.

`app/main.py`, `app/config/settings.py`, `app/models/toolbox.py`, `docs/14-dev-sre-toolbox.md`, `docs/README.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `.env.example` are listed in the approved plan but are not present in the supplied diff; documentation, OpenAPI `response_model` wiring, the new Settings fields and the `include_router` call are therefore unverified.

`requirements.txt` pins `PyYAML==6.0.3`; I cannot confirm from the diff that this exact version exists on PyPI (the latest I can recall is 6.0.2). If the pin is wrong the Docker build would fail even though the local test run passed. Verify the pin against the index.

Two different 422 shapes are produced: FastAPI's default `RequestValidationError` body for a structurally wrong outer request, and a custom `{"error": "Invalid tool input", "detail": [...]}` for a tool-input schema mismatch. The mandate says a structurally wrong request must follow the app's validation error handling; the inner-input 422 is a new shape and should be justified or aligned.

The router returns HTTP 504 on `asyncio.TimeoutError`, but 504 is not in the plan's `contracts` list (which documents 404/413/422/500). This is a deviation from the approved plan and is not covered by any test in the visible diff.

The `except ToolInputError` branch returns a 200 `ToolRunResponse` with `status="failed"` and a `TOOL_INPUT_ERROR` finding, but none of the three visible tools raises `ToolInputError`; the branch appears to be dead code and is untested. Either a tool should use it or it should be removed.

`max_findings` is enforced only after the full document loop completes (`if len(findings) > limits.max_findings: raise`), so the findings list can grow past the configured cap before the check fires. It is bounded by the input-size limit, but the check is post-hoc rather than incremental.

`asyncio.wait_for` around `loop.run_in_executor` cannot cancel the worker thread; on timeout the parsing thread keeps running. For bounded inputs this is acceptable, but it is a resource concern worth documenting.

No output-size limit is applied to `json.validate` (returns the full parsed value) or `text.diff` (returns the full diff). Large but under-limit inputs can produce large responses; the mandate only requires input limits, but this is worth an explicit note.
No visible test exercises the 504 timeout path, the `ToolInputError` path, or a 413 limit rejection through the k8s tool (the only 413 API test uses `json.validate`).
The test run reports 25 skipped tests; the diff does not show which suites are skipped, so I cannot confirm none of the toolbox tests are among them.

`_BoundedSafeLoader` enforces depth via recursive `compose_node`; if `toolbox_max_yaml_depth` is configured above Python's recursion limit, a deeply nested document could raise `RecursionError` instead of `ToolLimitExceeded`. The default value is not visible in the diff.
`text.diff` uses `splitlines()`, so inputs differing only in a trailing newline are reported as identical; this is a behavioural limitation that should be documented.

`_image_findings` treats any image string containing `@` as a digest reference; an image reference with `@` in a registry host would be misclassified. Low likelihood, but the heuristic is broader than `@sha256:`.

task-3a26188394573498.description: Add a self-contained `app/toolbox/` package (Tool protocol + explicit registry + three pure analysis functions), a thin `app/routers/toolbox.py` mounted at the repository's flat `/api/toolbox` prefix behind the existing `verify_credentials` Basic-Auth dependency, typed Pydantic models in `app/models/toolbox.py`, and env-driven limits in `app/config/settings.py`. One new dependency only: PyYAML, used exclusively through a custom `yaml.SafeLoader` subclass that enforces a nesting-depth budget and an alias/anchor expansion budget (so `toolbox_max_yaml_depth` is enforced during composition, not after parsing, and billion-laughs expansion is bounded). CPU-bound parsing is dispatched with `loop.run_in_executor` exactly as `/api/fib/{x}` already does, wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for` with a configurable timeout. No database, no queue, no migration, no new service, no new observability stack and no new metric families: run_id is correlation-only, logs go through the existing loguru setup, and invocation/error/duration visibility is already provided by the installed prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator. Controlled limit/unknown-tool errors are returned as explicit JSONResponse objects (413/404) so the app-wide 400/404 handlers cannot collapse them into `{"error": "Bad request"}` / `{"error": "Not found"}`. `json.validate` parses inline text only and does not use a URL/path prefix heuristic (the input schema has no URL/path field, so nothing is fetched or read).

handoff-2ca561c21501c4ac.initial_assessment:
Independent initial assessment of DEV1's candidate. The supplied diff is truncated: it begins mid-file inside the `responses` dict of `run_toolbox_tool` in `app/routers/toolbox.py`, so the router's imports, `_effective_limits()`, the `GET /tools` handler and the `APIRouter(prefix=..., dependencies=[Depends(verify_credentials)])` declaration are not visible. Also absent from the diff are `app/main.py`, `app/config/settings.py`, `app/models/toolbox.py`, `docs/14-dev-sre-toolbox.md`, `docs/README.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `.env.example`, all of which the approved plan lists as created/modified. My assessment therefore covers only the visible portion; the missing files are an evidence gap, not a proven defect (the initial checks show the app imports and the toolbox tests run, so `main.py`, `settings.py` and `models/toolbox.py` must exist and be wired).

What the visible code does well and matches the mandate: the toolbox is a self-contained `app/toolbox/` package with a `Tool` Protocol, an explicit import-time registry with a duplicate-id `RuntimeError`, and three pure-Python tools that never import FastAPI (`app/toolbox/base.py`, `registry.py`, `tools/*.py`). YAML is parsed through a `yaml.SafeLoader` subclass that enforces a composition-depth budget and an alias budget during composition, plus a cycle-aware `_assert_object_depth` walk over the composed graph; no `eval`/`exec`/shell/dynamic import/network/file access appears. Limits (input bytes, YAML documents, depth, aliases, findings, diff context lines) are carried in a frozen `ToolLimits` dataclass and exceeded limits raise `ToolLimitExceeded` (no silent truncation). The router dispatches `tool.run` via `loop.run_in_executor` wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for`, generates a `run_id`, logs `run_id/tool/status/outcome/duration_ms` without payload, and returns sanitized 500 (`run_id` only) and 404/413/422/504 as explicit `JSONResponse` objects so the app-wide 400/404 handlers cannot collapse them. Findings are returned inside a 200 `ToolRunResponse`, never as HTTP errors; invalid JSON and invalid YAML produce negative analysis results (`JSON_INVALID_SYNTAX`, `K8S_INVALID_YAML`) rather than HTTP errors. The k8s tool covers all seven mandated check families, distinguishes `missing_configuration` from `risky_configuration`, skips probe checks for init containers while still inspecting them, and carries a `DISCLAIMER` stating the checks are neither a complete Kubernetes validation nor a security certification. Initial checks report `project.build` PASS, `project.test` PASS (133 passed, 25 skipped), `project.lint` PASS (0).

Overall: the visible implementation is coherent, deterministic (only `run_id`/`duration_ms` vary), and consistent with the approved plan. I have not seen DEV1's handoff; the concerns below are the items I would want resolved or explicitly accepted before I can sign off, and several are unverifiable from the truncated diff.
